newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Endesa prepays World Bank loans in ecology spat.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Endesa prepays World Bank loans in ecology spat.

text.p: Chilean electricity giant Endesa said Tuesday it will prepay loans totalling $150 million to the World Bank following a spat over environmental obligations at the firm's controversial Pangue and Ralco dams.
"The decision ... was adopted after analysing different offers from international banks which offered better terms than the loan granted by the IFC," said the statement.
The International Finance Corp. (IFC), the private finance wing of the World Bank, was one of the main financiers behind the Pangue hydro-electric dam.

In a letter addressed last month to Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat, Bank President James Wolfensohn threated to declare Endesa in default of the loans and accused the firm of dragging its feet over preparing an environment impact study for Ralco.
IFC officials held meetings with Endesa officials this week to try and resolve the dispute over the dams that span the Bio Bio river in southern Chile.
The projects have raised vociferous protests from ecologists as they will flood large areas of the Bio Bio valley, forcing hundreds of Pehuenche Indians from their homes.
Endesa said it will prepay the loans using a new five-year credit from the Dresdner Bank which offered lower interest rates than the IFC agreement.
